use_case_summary: Deckhand is building a developer-focused pair-programming assistant embedded in IDEs and a browser extension. Primary workload is long-context chat (session transcripts + repo snapshot), plus low-latency inline completions. Expectation: mixed traffic with periodic high-concurrency peaks during dev sprints (20-50 concurrent users) and long context per-user (20k-100k tokens). Cost sensitivity: high (startup runway), prefers predictable per-token billing and suggestions to reduce unit cost (quantization, batching).
technical_requirements: - Long-context support >= 80k tokens; ability to stream partial completions to VSCode extension. - Reasonable latency for interactive completions (p50 < 250ms token-emit for short prompts). - Burst/Rate-limit guarantees or clear throttling behaviour for live sessions. - SDKs: first-class TypeScript + Python packages, lightweight browser SDK for extension. - Prefix/KV caching recommended for session reuse. - Simple rollback/version pinning for model updates.
security_and_compliance_notes: SMB but handling customer repos; requires SSO/SAML for internal user access, audit logs for admin console, minimal retention (30 days) for ephemeral session data. Asked for SOC2 compliance docs; sent link to security FAQ (drive).
pricing_and_financial_notes: Estimated ARR ask in small band (5k-25k). Interested in usage discounts once steady 3-6 month commit. Wants example bill for 50 daily active devs with avg 40k tokens/session. Asked for cost-savings suggestions (batching, caching, smaller model fallback).
sales_play_notes: PLG inbound; high product-fit. Recommended path: quick POC with hosted API -> show cost per session -> propose startup committed tier if POC successful. Keep engagement lightweight: one technical POC call + configurable trial quota. Emphasize SDKs and streaming demos for VSCode integration.
